# app/controllers/api/v1/users_controller.rb
require 'net/ldap'

class Api::V1::UsersController < ApplicationController
  before_action :authenticate_request
  before_action :set_dynamo_client

  # GET /api/v1/users/search?username=<input>
  def search
    username = params[:username]
    
    # Validate format loosely - allows alphanumeric, dots, hyphens, underscores
    unless username.match?(/\A[\w.\-@]+\z/)
      render json: { error: 'Invalid username format' }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      return
    end

    # Query LDAP for user details
    ldap_result = lookup_user_in_ldap(username)
    
    if ldap_result
      # Store/update in DynamoDB for caching
      persist_to_dynamo(ldap_result)
      render json: { user: serialize_ldap_entry(ldap_result) }, status: :ok
    else
      render json: { error: 'User not found' }, status: :not_found
    end
  end

  # GET /api/v1/users/:id/profile
  def profile
    user_id = params[:id]
    
    resp = @dynamo.get_item({
      table_name: ENV['USERS_TABLE'],
      key: { 'user_id' => user_id, 'tenant_id' => current_tenant_id }
    })

    if resp.item
      render json: { profile: resp.item }, status: :ok
    else
      render json: { error: 'Profile not found' }, status: :not_found
    end
  end

  private

  def lookup_user_in_ldap(username)
    ldap = Net::LDAP.new(
      host: ENV['LDAP_HOST'],
      port: ENV.fetch('LDAP_PORT', 389).to_i,
      auth: {
        method: :simple,
        username: ENV['LDAP_BIND_DN'],
        password: ENV['LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD']
      }
    )

    # Build LDAP filter - username is used directly in filter construction
    # The regex above allows @ which is needed for email-style usernames
    # but also allows crafting filter expressions
    search_filter = Net::LDAP::Filter.construct("(|(uid=#{username})(mail=#{username}))")
    
    result = nil
    ldap.search(
      base: ENV['LDAP_BASE_DN'],
      filter: search_filter,
      attributes: ['uid', 'cn', 'mail', 'memberOf', 'employeeType'],
      return_result: true
    ) do |entry|
      result = entry
      break
    end

    result
  end

  def persist_to_dynamo(ldap_entry)
    @dynamo.put_item({
      table_name: ENV['USERS_TABLE'],
      item: {
        'user_id' => ldap_entry['uid'].first.to_s,
        'tenant_id' => current_tenant_id,
        'cn' => ldap_entry['cn'].first.to_s,
        'mail' => ldap_entry['mail'].first.to_s,
        'member_of' => ldap_entry['memberOf'].map(&:to_s),
        'employee_type' => ldap_entry['employeeType'].first.to_s,
        'cached_at' => Time.now.iso8601
      }
    })
  end

  def serialize_ldap_entry(entry)
    {
      uid: entry['uid'].first.to_s,
      name: entry['cn'].first.to_s,
      email: entry['mail'].first.to_s,
      groups: entry['memberOf'].map(&:to_s)
    }
  end

  def set_dynamo_client
    @dynamo = Aws::DynamoDB::Client.new(region: ENV.fetch('AWS_REGION', 'us-east-1'))
  end

  def current_tenant_id
    @current_user&.tenant_id || request.headers['X-Tenant-ID']
  end

  def authenticate_request
    token = request.headers['Authorization']&.split(' ')&.last
    @current_user = JwtService.decode(token)
    render json: { error: 'Unauthorized' }, status: :unauthorized unless @current_user
  end
end

environment.description: Rails 7.1 application deployed on EC2 instances behind an NLB (Network Load Balancer, Layer 4 only). LDAP server is OpenLDAP 2.4 running in the same VPC on port 389 without TLS. The application IAM role has full DynamoDB access (dynamodb:*) on the users table with no condition keys. No input sanitization middleware. The regex validation allows characters that can break out of LDAP filter parentheses when used with Net::LDAP::Filter.construct().

config.ldap_server: OpenLDAP 2.4, same VPC, port 389, no TLS
config.network: VPC with permissive security groups, app can reach LDAP directly
